articles.title: Acute-on-Chronic Liver Failure: Definitions, Management, Prognostication, and Transplantation.
articles.abstract: Acute-on-chronic liver failure is a rapidly evolving syndrome characterized by acute decompensation, organ failure, and high short-term mortality. This article reviews international definitions, epidemiology, pathophysiology, diagnostic evaluation, critical-care management, prognostic models, liver transplantation (LT), posttransplant risk assessment, palliative care, current controversies, and emerging research. The recommended clinical approach emphasizes prompt identification of reversible precipitants, evidence-based organ support, serial assessment of disease trajectory during the first week, early referral for LT evaluation when appropriate, and alignment of treatment intensity with prognosis and patient preferences.
articles.authors: Yagan Lina, Mohan Rahul, Hernaez Ruben

articles.title: Critical Care Management of Disaster-Related Organ Failure.
articles.abstract: Disasters generate high volumes of multisystem trauma while simultaneously degrading the staff, equipment, and electricity that critical care depends on. This article reviews management of disaster-related organ failure under resource constraint. It outlines step-wise respiratory support, from high-flow nasal cannula and noninvasive ventilation to lung-protective mechanical ventilation; prevention and treatment of acute kidney injury (AKI), including dialysis options for AKI and end-stage renal disease patients; recognition of hemorrhagic, neurogenic, cardiogenic, and obstructive shock; and secondary complications including coagulopathy, hypothermia, abdominal compartment syndrome, hepatic dysfunction, and hyperglycemia. Ethical triage, palliation, telecritical care, and staffing models are also addressed.
articles.source: The Surgical clinics of North America
articles.authors: Hertel Kristie, Bard Michael

articles.title: Rehabilitation in the Intensive Care Unit: Preparing Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation Professionals to Support Biopsychosocial Well-Being.
articles.abstract: With medical advances, more critically ill patients survive and often experience new or worsening physical, cognitive, and/or mental health sequelae. The intensive care unit involves interdisciplinary survival-focused care, and its biopsychosocial impact is profound and long-lasting. In this article, we have highlighted the World Health Organization's International Classification of Functioning as a person-centered, holistic, and contextually grounded framework for early rehabilitation specifically for critical care survivorship. The goal of this article is to elucidate the key role of physical medicine and rehabilitation professionals in enhancing the recovery trajectory of critical illness survivors within a transdiagnostic, interdisciplinary framework.
articles.source: Physical medicine and rehabilitation clinics of North America
articles.authors: Merbitz Nancy, Hampton Jessica M, Mladen Samantha N, et al.

articles.title: Intraosseous Vascular Access.
articles.abstract: Intraosseous (IO) vascular access is a high-yield bedside procedure for adult inpatient and critical care medicine. When deployed early in high-acuity situations, IO access provides rapid, reliable central vascular access with high success rates and very rare major complications. Effective use requires appropriate site and needle selection, multimodal confirmation of appropriate placement, and vigilant monitoring for extravasation and neurovascular compromise. In awake patients, analgesia, including consideration of IO lidocaine before the initial flush, improves tolerance. IO-derived laboratory results can be useful when no alternative access exists but should be treated as provisional and confirmed once definitive access is secured.
articles.source: The Medical clinics of North America
articles.authors: Voronina Angelina, Freidinger Alexander G, Lords Allie, et al.

articles.title: Prediction, Prescription, and Proactive Medication Management in the Intensive Care Unit.
articles.abstract: This narrative review examines the evolving role of prediction analytics in comprehensive medication management for critically ill patients. Intensive care unit pharmacotherapy is challenged by medication complexity, physiologic instability, heterogeneous treatment response, and continuous data streams. Predictive systems may support proactive medication management by identifying medication-related harm, therapeutic failure, optimization opportunities, and pharmacist workload earlier in the patient trajectory. The review discusses medication-informed prediction models, prescriptive analytics, workload-aware critical care pharmacist allocation, and potential future applications. Implementation requires actionable predictions, workflow integration, clinician oversight, and attention to equity, safety, and model credibility.
articles.authors: Murray Brian

articles.title: Intensive Monitoring, Big Data, and Artificial Intelligence in Critical Care.
articles.abstract: Intensive care is defined by providing a higher level of patient monitoring, but only a fraction of the data created through continuous hemodynamic monitoring are captured in the electronic health record. The monitoring data that is captured misses clinically important deterioration events and is not adequate to represent critical illness physiology for care at the bedside or for research. This article describes the current state of patient monitoring in intensive care, advanced monitors in development, metadata and its role in creating rich intensive care data sources, and machine learning and its current and future applications in intensive care medicine.
articles.authors: Rzewnicki Daniel I, Bhavani Sivasubramanium V

articles.title: Redesigning Intensive Care Unit Workflows: A Learning Health System Approach to Improving Care Delivery.
articles.abstract: Critical care leaders are increasingly asked to improve outcomes, reduce burden, and implement evidence-based care in complex, highly interdependent clinical environments. Meeting this challenge requires redesigning the workflows through which care is delivered, not simply measuring outcomes or adding new tools. This article presents a learning health system model that integrates sociotechnical systems thinking, quality improvement, health services research, and informatics to support workflow redesign. Multidimensional workflow signals inform the Diagnose, Redesign, Implement, Verify, Evolve (DRIVE) cycle to make care delivery more reliable, less burdensome, and better aligned with outcomes that matter to patients.
articles.authors: Murphy David J

articles.title: Optimizing Team Integration of Critical Care Pharmacists: Where We Go Next.
articles.abstract: Critical care pharmacists (CCPs) are essential members of the intensive care unit team who provide comprehensive medication management to improve patient outcomes, safety, and cost efficiency. This article highlights barriers to optimal integration of CCPs within multidisciplinary teams as well as opportunities to address them. Persistent barriers include financial, workforce, data, interprofessional, and regulatory. Strategies to address these gaps may involve standardized metrics, innovative staffing models, and research to strengthen evidence-based implementation. Metrics should include all members of the Stakeholder Triad and should include a mix of workload metrics, safety and efficacy metrics, and work-design metrics.
articles.authors: Smith Susan E, Henry Kelli, Papadopoulos John, et al.

articles.title: Optimizing Team Integration of Critical Care Pharmacists: A History of Critical Care Pharmacy Practice and Evolving Definition of "Optimal Practice".
articles.abstract: Critical Care Pharmacists (CCPs) are essential members of the intensive care unit (ICU) team who provide comprehensive medication management to improve patient outcomes, safety, and cost efficiency. This article highlights best practices for optimal CCP integration, including optimal patient-to-pharmacist ratios, participation in interprofessional rounds, team-based practice models, and expanded coverage across all shifts. The Triple Domain framework is useful to evaluate CCP value across patients, health care teams, and institutions. Best practices include an ICU patient-to-CCP ratio of less than or equal to 15:1 and inclusion of CCPs on daily interprofessional rounds.
articles.authors: Smith Susan E, Bektas Aeryana N, Henry Kelli, et al.

articles.title: The COVID-19 Pandemic as a Stress Test of the Intensive Care Unit Workforce.
articles.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic monumentally strained the intensive care unit (ICU) workforce and revealed both the strengths and vulnerabilities in contemporary critical care delivery. In this review, we briefly describe the composition of the US ICU workforce and the organizational features most relevant to staffing. Next, we examine how the pandemic disrupted critical care delivery, specifically health care workers. Finally, we discuss the lasting psychological toll and workforce attrition; highlight adaptations that emerged, such as tele-ICU expansion, virtual family engagement, tiered staffing models, rapid-onboarding curricula, and peer support programs; and outline priorities for policy, practice, and research to strengthen workforce resilience.
articles.authors: Connell Kathryn A, Vranas Kelly C, Yu Hyunmin, et al.

articles.title: The Intensive Care Unit Team: Roles, Scope, and Interprofessional Interdependence in the Intensive Care Unit.
articles.abstract: A hallmark feature of an intensive care unit (ICU) is the presence of a structured team-based interprofessional model. Although composition of the ICU team varies by organization and patient population, it typically includes critical care nurses, intensivists, respiratory therapists, and clinical pharmacists. Interprofessional teams in ICUs are associated with increased collaboration and improved patient outcomes. However, the ICU team faces challenges in workforce shortages, staffing gaps, and ineffective information sharing, which can inhibit effective team function. Proven strategies to support collaboration among the ICU team include structured interprofessional rounds, strong leadership of the team, care protocols, and quality bundles.
articles.authors: Manzo Laura L, Christoph Ella N I, Kessinger Stephanie K, et al.

articles.title: External hydrocephalus in adult neurocritical patients.
articles.abstract: External hydrocephalus (EH) in adults is an underrecognized clinical entity characterized by CSF circulatory failure and progressive subarachnoid space (SAS) dilation under high intracranial pressure (ICP). Data regarding its incidence, pathophysiology, and management in adult neurocritical care are sparse. To describe the incidence, risk factors and outcome of EH in adult neurocritical patients. Prospective study of patients with moderate-to-severe traumatic brain injury (msTBI) or spontaneous subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) admitted to intensive care unit (ICU). Three subgroups ere defined: 1) radiological EH: dilated SAS between two successive CT scans; 2) radiological EH in the context of intracranial hypertension (IH): suspected o confirmed elevated ICP; and 3) radiological EH and invasively documented elevated ICP. A total of 128 patients were included (78 msTBI, 50 SAH). The incidence of radiological EH was 20.3 % (26.9 % in msTBI and 10 % in SAH), while the incidence of radiological EH in the context of IH was 7.8 % (10.3 % in msTBI vs. 4 % in SAH). The median time to EH onset was 4.5. Radiological EH in the context of IH was significantly associated with younger age, refract
articles.source: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
articles.authors: Grille Pedro, Lecor Emiliano, Bouzas Pablo

articles.title: Streamlining the Evidence-to-Practice Pathway With Computerised Decision Support in Anaesthesiology and Critical Care: A Qualitative Study of Clinician and System-Level Interest Holder Perspectives Across Five Scandinavian Countries.
articles.abstract: Implementing evidence-based recommendations in anaesthesiology and critical care remains challenging due to guideline, workflow and contextual barriers. Guideline-based computerised clinical decision support systems (CDSS), embedded in structured pathways linking international guidelines to Scandinavian-endorsed recommendations and delivered via electronic health records, may help strengthen the evidence-to-practice pathway. This study aimed to explore perceived barriers and facilitators to their use. This qualitative study interviewed 10 clinicians (anaesthesiologists and intensivists; specialists and non-specialists; < 40 and ≥ 40 years; male and female) and nine system-level stakeholders (hospital and health authority representatives) from Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway and Sweden. We integrated endorsed international guidelines into a CDSS providing patient-specific reminders linked to recommendations, as well as shared decision-making tools and decision-analytic components. Using a simulation application, participants explored the CDSS in a demo electronic health record. Through a framework analysis based on the GUIDES checklist, we categorised perspectives as barriers, fac
articles.authors: Van de Velde Stijn, Seterelv Siri, Kunnamo Ilkka, et al.

articles.title: A Survey of Clinician-Reported Management of Hypernatremia in the ICU.
articles.abstract: Hypernatremia is frequent in the intensive care unit (ICU) and is associated with adverse outcomes. Despite its prevalence, robust evidence to guide treatment is lacking, and global practice patterns are largely unknown. We investigated global treatment preferences and clinicians' willingness to enroll patients in a randomized trial to inform its feasibility. This international cross-sectional online survey comprised 20 primarily closed-ended questions, using five-point Likert-scale responses, across four themes: treatment method, threshold, correction rate, and opinion on a proposed trial. Respondents considered a clinical vignette of hypernatremia developing before or during ICU admission, excluding dehydration and chronic causes. It was distributed to ICU physicians worldwide. The survey was sent to 3053 ICU physicians in 17 countries, with 1051 respondents, yielding a response rate of 34%. Of respondents, 74% were consultants, and 26% were residents. The mean ICU experience was 14 years. Increasing free water intake via enteral route was the most frequently reported treatment strategy (80% reporting "often" or "always"). articles.authors: Seitz-Rasmussen Hans Eric Sebastian, Bestle Morten H, Schjørring Olav Lilleholt, et al.

articles.title: Serious Adverse Events in Adult ICU Patients: A Substudy of the PATIENCE Cohort.
articles.abstract: Prokinetic agents are used to enhance upper gastrointestinal motility, but adverse events related to these agents are poorly described. We aimed to provide detailed epidemiological data on predefined serious adverse events (SAEs) in a cohort of adult intensive care unit (ICU) patients with and without prokinetic treatment. We hypothesised that all predefined SAEs would occur in both patients treated and those not treated with prokinetic agents, and that a higher number of SAEs would occur among patients treated with prokinetic agents for more than three consecutive days. This substudy of the inception cohort study "Prokinetic agents in adult intensive care unit patients" included acutely admitted adult ICU patients. The prokinetic agents assessed (exposures) were erythromycin, metoclopramide, domperidone, and prucalopride. The primary outcome was the proportion of patients experiencing at least one episode of five pre-specified SAEs during ICU stay (cardiac arrhythmias, cardiac arrest, vomiting with aspiration, diarrhoea, extrapyramidal symptoms). Secondary outcomes were (1) proportion of patients experiencing each SAE, (2) the proportion of patients experiencing any of the SAEs af
articles.authors: Crone Vera, Møller Morten Hylander, Granholm Anders, et al.

articles.title: Discussing Future Treatment and Care in the ICU: Perspectives From Patients.
articles.abstract: Treatment in the intensive care unit (ICU) is usually predicated on curative treatment, but continuing all available treatment options may not always be beneficial for the patient or in line with their wishes. However, patients admitted to the ICU are often assessed as incapable of making decisions regarding their care; hence conversations about wishes for treatment are postponed. This study aimed to investigate the experiences of patients who participated in a conversation concerning treatment and care following ICU discharge based on the Danish version of the Recommended Summary Plan for Emergency Care and Treatment (ReSPECT) form. Semi-structured telephone interviews were conducted with patients who had a conversation about future treatment and care with an intensivist using the ReSPECT form during an ICU admission between November 2024 and July 2025. Relatives who participated in the conversation and were present during the interviews were asked to elaborate on their experiences of the conversation's timing and how they felt about participating in the conversation. Data was analysed using content analysis. Nineteen patients were included in the study, of whom 15 patients (83%)
articles.authors: Smith Mette A, Zwisler Ann Dorthe, Nissen Anne, et al.

articles.title: Swedish Consensus Recommendation for Follow-Up After ICU Stay.
articles.abstract: A substantial proportion of intensive care unit (ICU) survivors experience long-term physical, psychological and cognitive impairments after critical illness. However, methods for identifying patients in need of post-ICU support vary widely. As a result, many patients are left without access to established rehabilitation pathways. This consensus recommendation provides a framework for the organisation and content of follow-up for adult ICU survivors in Sweden, informed by available evidence, stakeholder perspectives and expert consensus. The National System for Knowledge-Driven Healthcare Management (NPO) in Sweden commissioned the development of a practice recommendation for the follow-up of critically ill adults. Multidisciplinary experts in ICU survivorship formed a task force group. A systematic literature search in four databases was conducted in 2024 to identify pre-existing systematic reviews on the topic. The literature was reviewed, assessed for quality and recommendations were developed based on the literature evidence. The draft was discussed among multiprofessional groups involved in follow-up, in workshops with critical care nurses (n = 30) and professionals responsibl
articles.authors: Åkerman Eva, Schandl Anna, Ringdal Mona, et al.

articles.title: Pressure injury prevention in critical care: A reflexive thematic analysis of clinicians' perspectives on complexity and clinical judgement.
articles.abstract: Pressure injury prevention in critical care remains a persistent global challenge. Despite established guidelines, implementation is often constrained by physiological instability, device burden, and competing clinical priorities. Emerging digital and artificial intelligence approaches offer potential support, yet their role within the complexity of critical care practice remains unclear. To explore clinicians' perspectives on pressure injury prevention in critical care, with particular attention to complexity, clinical decision-making and the potential role of emerging technologies. Qualitative study using reflexive thematic analysis. We analysed 12 brief written reflections from clinicians working in critical care and related roles, predominantly in the United Kingdom. We purposively invited contributors through professional networks, who responded to shared prompts on prevention challenges, practice tensions, and potential roles for artificial intelligence. The first author led iterative semantic and latent coding within a contextualist-constructionist reflexive thematic analysis, supported by reflexive discussion among the author team. articles.authors: Johnson Gideon U, You HyunBin, Trotta Francesca, et al.

articles.title: Metabolic dysfunction in chronic critical illness: mechanisms, clinical consequences and therapeutic perspectives.
articles.abstract: Advances in intensive care have improved survival from acute critical illness, leading to a growing population of patients with chronic critical illness (CCI), many of whom require prolonged organ support. This condition is associated with persistent catabolism, inflammation, and poor long-term outcomes. Understanding the metabolic alterations underlying this failure to recover may help identify targets for monitoring and intervention. This review synthesizes current clinical and translational evidence on metabolic dysregulation in CCI and discusses its implications for monitoring, nutritional strategies, and therapeutic interventions. We performed a narrative review informed by a structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE followed by manual reference screening. Preclinical, translational and clinical studies addressing energy metabolism, mitochondrial function, autophagy, ketone metabolism, inflammation and recovery trajectories in critical illness were qualitatively synthesized. articles.authors: Castro Sílvia, Granja Cristina, Dionne Joanna C, et al.

articles.title: How are researchers using MIMIC? A sampling-based methods review.
articles.abstract: The Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC) database is a widely used open data resource in critical care research. Its accessibility has led to large numbers of research studies being published; however, design and analysis decisions made by individual studies may vary, affecting comparability and reproducibility. We conducted a sampling-based methods review of research that analysed the MIMIC database. Studies published between 2015 and 2025 were eligible for inclusion in the sampling frame. A random sample of 100 eligible studies was identified through the OpenAlex bibliographic database; data were collected using a structured extraction framework. Information was extracted on study aims, cohort definitions, exclusion criteria, outcome specification, handling of missing data, and analytical methods. The review focused on how key design and analytical decisions were reported and justified in the random sample. Studies reported findings from general ICU and specific clinical populations; the study population could not be determined for 32 of the 100 studies. Sixty studies addressed predictive research questions, but only one predictive study reporting external validati
articles.authors: Kenarangi Tayyebeh, Barnett Adrian, Suen Jacky Yung, et al.

articles.title: Analysis of work system components in interprofessional communication to determine shock etiology.
articles.abstract: In critical care settings, lack of agreement among clinicians on shock etiology is associated with higher mortality. Effective interprofessional communication may facilitate agreement on etiology and reduce mortality. This study sought to understand the interaction of work system components (people, environments, tools, tasks) in interprofessional communication to determine shock etiology. We interviewed 28 physicians, advanced practice providers, nurses, and pharmacists at three United States hospitals using a Critical Incident Technique. Analysis was guided by the Systems Engineering Initiative for Patient Safety model. The principal finding was that clinicians worked across fragmented physical, socio-organizational, and digital environments to balance the urgency to treat shock with intermediate steps to reduce diagnostic uncertainty. The results suggest that future research should acknowledge the benefits of productive disagreement among clinicians and develop supports that promote synchronous communication by bridging physical and socio-organizational fragmentation, compiling and systematizing relevant clinical information, and generating shared awareness among clinicians.
articles.authors: Cong Lixuan, Abahuje Egide, Slocum John D, et al.

articles.title: Training of trainers on medical education reforms: a prospective multicenter French survey among intensivists.
articles.abstract: The recent reform of the second cycle of medical education in France introduced competency-based medical education (CBME) with the incorporation of several pedagogical modalities into undergraduate training and assessment, including objective structured clinical examinations (OSCEs), simulation-based teaching (SBT), and clinical reasoning (CR) instruction throughout the academic year. While these tools are central to preparing competent practitioners, their effective implementation depends on adequately trained educators. We hypothesized that training would be insufficient, notably in the recently introduced pedagogical modalities. We conducted a national, cross-sectional survey (June-September 2023) to assess the level and adequacy of training of board-certified physicians practicing in critical care and involved in undergraduate teaching. An anonymous online questionnaire collected demographic data, teaching frequency, training characteristics, perceived adequacy and usefulness of training, preparedness, and barriers. The responses were analyzed descriptively and comparatively. Among the 151 eligible respondents (72% male, median age 41 years, 70% working in teaching hospitals, a
articles.authors: Hermann Bertrand, Truchot Jennifer, Cariou Alain, et al.

articles.title: Beyond the ICU: family resilience and emotional turmoil after intensive care - a qualitative study.
articles.abstract: During the COVID-19 pandemic, visitation restrictions in ICUs intensified psychological distress among family members, yet the long-term impact of psychosocial support on family resilience remains poorly understood. To evaluate the experiences of family members during the COVID-19 pandemic, focusing on interactions with healthcare professionals and well-being 18th months after hospitalisation. A qualitative descriptive study using semi-structured interviews with 14 families of patients admitted to the ICU in spring 2020.Data were analysed using inductive content analysis. Experiences were shaped by caring interactions with healthcare professionals, emotional disruption, and reliance on family support. Clear information and psychosocial support fostered trust but were also associated with stress and feelings of isolation. The experience caused profound emotional distress, with family members reporting lasting anxiety, while others described gratitude and personal growth. Support from Family were central to coping, although the responsibility as the primary contact person could increase emotional burden. articles.source: International journal of qualitative studies on health and well-being
articles.authors: Lönnkvist Jenny, Lundberg Tina, Åkerman Eva, et al.

articles.title: Intensive Care Unit Management of the Hemodynamically Significant Pulmonary Embolism.
articles.abstract: Acute pulmonary embolism remains a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, with prognosis determined by right ventricular (RV) adaptation to the abrupt rise in pulmonary vascular resistance. Although most cases can be managed outside the intensive care unit, patients with RV failure, hemodynamic instability, or cardiac arrest require advanced monitoring and intervention. Management in this setting emphasizes rapid diagnosis and risk stratification, timely initiation of reperfusion therapies, and carefully tailored hemodynamic and respiratory support. Optimal outcomes rely on multidisciplinary collaboration, early escalation of care, and individualized, evidence-based decision-making.
articles.authors: Ehret Jane, Langston Matthew D, Friedman Oren

articles.title: Higher Daily Hospitalization Costs and Intensive Care Utilization Among Decedents With Systemic Lupus Erythematosus and Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Bioethical Analysis of End-of-Life Care.
articles.abstract: End-of-life care creates financial burdens. This study examines medical procedures/interventions and costs for inpatients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and rheumatoid arthritis (RA), comparing those who died during hospitalization to those who survived, analyzing the findings through a bioethical perspective. This observational 1:1 case-control study was conducted at a tertiary care center. Patients with SLE and RA (ICD-10-CM diagnostic codes) who were hospitalized for at least 24 h during two distinct periods-January-June 2019 and January-June 2023-were included. Patients were designated as cases if they died during hospitalization and as controls if they were discharged alive. Data were abstracted from electronic medical records using standardized formats. Microcosting data for each hospitalization were obtained from the accounting department. We identified 29 matched pairs of cases and controls, primarily comprising middle-aged females, with SLE. Cases and controls had similar sociodemographic and disease-related characteristics. articles.source: Journal of evaluation in clinical practice
articles.authors: Guaracha-Basañez Guillermo Arturo, Contreras-Yáñez Irazú, Jiménez-Decle Julia Giselle, et al.

articles.title: Consent for intensive care research involving adults who lack decision-making capacity: A jurisdictional analysis of Australia's fragmented framework.
articles.abstract: Critically ill adults frequently cannot consent to research because of sedation, delirium, shock or mechanical ventilation, yet safe intensive care depends on evidence generated in this population; several treatments once regarded as standard care proved harmful when finally tested in randomised trials. The ethical framework for enrolling adults who lack decision-making capacity is national-the National Health and Medical Research Council National Statement on Ethical Conduct in Human Research (2025), in effect since 23 June 2026-but legal authority for substitute consent is conferred by eight state and territory statutes that differ in terminology, in decision-maker hierarchies, in whether they address research at all, and whether they permit enrolment in an emergency. Mapping four representative study archetypes across all eight jurisdictions shows that the lawful basis for enrolling the same patient shifts with study design as much as with geography; differing statutory definitions, tribunal involvement and the transition to the 2025 National Statement produce material and avoidable inconsistency. articles.authors: Bihari Shailesh, Galluccio Steven, McIntyre JoAnne, et al.

articles.title: Kidney effects of inhaled nitric oxide in critically ill patients: from pathophysiological considerations to clinical implications.
articles.abstract: Inhaled nitric oxide is widely used as a selective pulmonary vasodilator in critical care, yet its renal effects remain controversial. While existing reviews mostly focus on indications for inhaled nitric oxide and its impact on outcomes, limited data exist on its renal effects, since it was thought to act only locally in the lungs. This review examine the clinical evidence regarding kidney outcomes associated with inhaled nitric oxide across major indications and provide an integrated mechanistic analysis of nitric oxide signaling in renal physiology and pathophysiology. Nitric oxide is produced by nitric oxide synthases using L-arginine as a substrate. It acts as a smooth muscle relaxation factor and ultimately causes vasodilation through its effect on cyclic guanosine monophosphate. Nitric oxide plays a pivotal role in renal hemodynamic regulation, glomerular filtration, tubular function, and microcirculatory homeostasis. The net renal effect of inhaled nitric oxide likely reflects the balance between improved nitric oxide signaling and oxidative stress generation. articles.authors: Robert Arnaud, Gonze Aurélien, Bulpa Pierre, et al.

articles.title: Short-chain fatty acid metabolism in acute lung injury and intervention strategies from traditional Chinese medicine.
articles.abstract: Acute lung injury (ALI) and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) are severe conditions associated with high mortality rates and limited treatment options. Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) serve as central immunomodulatory metabolites mediate the crosstalk between the gut and lung. Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), with its holistic approach, shows promise in restoring gut-lung balance and alleviating respiratory inflammation by modulating gut microbiota and SCFA metabolism. To elucidate the protective role and mechanism of SCFAs in ALI and ARDS via the gut-lung axis. Meanwhile, to evaluate the therapeutic potential of TCM in treating ALI by modulating the gut microbiota and enhancing SCFA production. A comprehensive literature search was conducted across PubMed, Ovid-Embase, Web of Science, and CNKI databases (2010-2025). Keywords included "short-chain fatty acid", "gut microbes", "acute lung injury", "traditional Chinese medicine", and related terms. The search focused on preclinical and mechanistic studies investigating SCFA signaling, gut microbiota remodeling, and the therapeutic effects of herbal compounds or their active constituents in ALI/ARDS models. articles.authors: Zhao Bing, Li Rongrong, Chen Dandan, et al.

articles.title: Effects of Iloprost on Nitric Oxide Biomarkers in Patients With Septic Shock and Severe Endotheliopathy.
articles.abstract: Septic shock is characterized by profound endothelial dysfunction, which may involve changes in the prostacyclin and nitric oxide (NO) pathways and contribute to immune dysregulation, coagulopathy, and vascular instability. Iloprost has shown potential to modulate NO biomarkers in non-septic conditions. We investigated whether treatment with the prostacyclin analog iloprost affected plasma concentrations of the NO biomarkers ADMA, SDMA, arginine, and homoarginine in patients with septic shock and severe endotheliopathy. This preplanned sub-study of the randomized, blinded COMBAT-SHINE trial enrolled 274 adult ICU patients with septic shock and severe endotheliopathy (defined as soluble thrombomodulin (sTM) > 10 ng/mL) who had consented to the use of data. Five participants from the full trial population withdrew consent. Participants were allocated to a 72-h infusion of iloprost (1 ng/kg/min) versus placebo. Plasma concentrations of ADMA, SDMA, arginine, and homoarginine were measured at 0, 24, 48, and 72 h. Changes in biomarker concentrations were assessed using linear mixed models, with predefined subgroup analyses. All results were considered exploratory. In explorative analyses
articles.authors: Mortensen Karoline Myglegård, Itenov Theis Skovsgaard, Stensballe Jakob, et al.

articles.title: Effect of pneumatic leg compression on post-induction hypotension in adult patients with isolated traumatic brain injury undergoing decompressive craniotomy: a randomised, double-blind, controlled trial.
articles.abstract: Post-induction hypotension is common after induction of general anaesthesia, and in traumatic brain injury even a brief fall in systemic pressure can compromise cerebral perfusion when autoregulation is already impaired. Pneumatic leg compression augments venous return and has reduced post-induction hypotension in obstetric and urological surgery, but has not been examined in neurotrauma patients undergoing decompressive craniotomy. In this prospective, randomised, double-blind trial, adults aged 18-65 years with isolated traumatic brain injury and radiological features of severity (midline shift ≥5 mm with basal cistern effacement) undergoing decompressive craniotomy were allocated 1:1 to a pneumatic compression device activated before induction (Group PC) or an identical device left inactive (Group NC). The primary outcome was the incidence of post-induction hypotension, defined as any recorded one-minute systolic blood pressure below 90 mmHg within 20 minutes of induction. Secondary outcomes included the haemodynamic trend, fluid and vasopressor requirement, arterial blood gas changes, and device-related complications up to 72 hours. Analysis was by modified intention-to-treat.
articles.source: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
articles.authors: Ahlawat Vidushi, Pandey Vaibhav, Luthra Ankur, et al.

articles.title: The predictive value of early clinical and electrodiagnostic markers on short- and long-term functional outcomes in Guillain-Barré Syndrome: a systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Guillain-Barré Syndrome (GBS) presents with highly variable recovery trajectories. Early identification of prognostic markers is crucial for optimizing patient management and anticipating severe complications. A systematic search of PubMed, EMBASE, and Scopus was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Studies reporting early clinical or electrodiagnostic predictors of functional outcomes in confirmed GBS patients were eligible. Study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment were each performed independently and in duplicate by both authors (PYG and JHW). Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Exploratory meta-analyses were performed using standardized mean differences (SMD) for functional recovery and pooled proportions for mechanical ventilation incidence. Effect sizes were oriented so that a positive SMD consistently denotes poorer functional status in the poor-prognosis group. Functional recovery was additionally stratified a posteriori by outcome assessment timepoint (short-term, 1-4 weeks; long-term, 3-6 months). Seven studies (n = 398 patients) were included. articles.title: Herpesvirus reactivation in critical illness: Pathogenesis, clinical consequences, and diagnostic challenges.
articles.abstract: Human herpesviruses (HHV) remain latent after primary infection and may reactivate during critical illness. HHV reactivation has been associated with adverse clinical outcomes, yet its pathogenic significance and optimal management remain unclear. This review summarizes the dysregulated immune mechanisms and risk factors for HHV reactivation in critical illness, treatment options, outcomes, current diagnostic challenges, and emerging precision medicine approaches. Critical illness induces profound immune dysregulation characterized by an initial hyperinflammatory response followed by immunosuppression, T-cell exhaustion, impaired natural killer cell function, and disrupted antiviral surveillance. These changes facilitate reactivation of latent HHV, including herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1), cytomegalovirus (CMV), Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), and human herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6). HSV and CMV reactivation in mechanically ventilated and septic patients have been associated with prolonged mechanical ventilation, longer intensive care unit (ICU) stay, secondary infections, and increased mortality. articles.title: Cross-kingdom microbiome interactions along the gut-lung axis: immune-microecological coordination, shared mechanisms, and disease-context dependence in respiratory disorders.
articles.abstract: Cross-kingdom dysbiosis of the gut microbiome along the gut-lung axis has emerged as a key driver of chronic and acute respiratory diseases. Beyond bacteria, the intestinal mycobiome and virome, including bacteriophages, shape mucosal immunity and metabolism through partially overlapping but non-redundant pathways. In this Review, we synthesize rapidly expanding evidence that fungi, bacteria, and phages in the gut form an integrated network that may influence susceptibility, inflammatory tone, and therapeutic responsiveness across asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and lung cancer via the gut-lung axis. We first summarize how cross-kingdom communities in the intestine are organized and interact, highlighting a tripartite framework centered on pathogen-associated molecular pattern-pattern recognition receptor (PAMP-PRR) circuits, the short-chain fatty acid (SCFA)-regulatory T-cell axis, and tryptophan-indole-aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) signaling. Abnormal shear stress, mechanical stretch, pressure loading and tissue deformation continuously reshape the local mechanical microenvironment. articles.title: Prevalence and prognostic significance of respiratory failure before or at liver transplantation in acute-on-chronic liver failure: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Respiratory failure (RF) is an important organ failure phenotype in acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF), but its prevalence and prognostic significance among liver transplant (LT) recipients remain uncertain. We searched PubMed, Embase, and the Web of Science Core Collection for observational studies through August 17, 2026. Of 33 included study reports, clinically comparable data were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis; other evidence was synthesized narratively. Pooled RF prevalence was 7.5% (95% CI: 2.1%-23.0%) at earlier pretransplant assessment, 13.5% (5.7%-28.5%) among recipients with EASL-CLIF ACLF assessed on the day of LT, and 28.9% (9.7%-60.6%) among recipients with ACLF-3 assessed near LT. A broad analysis of 21 reports yielded 12.9% (9.0%-18.1%; 95% prediction interval: 3.3%-38.9%). Across three independent cohorts, pooled 1-year post-LT survival was 55.3% (20.0%-86.0%) in RF-positive recipients and 82.1% (66.9%-91.2%) in RF-negative recipients. RF-positive recipients had higher 1-year mortality (unadjusted RR = 2.41, 95% CI: 1.50-3.90). articles.title: The Pharmacologic Management of Cardiac Arrest.
articles.abstract: The effectiveness of pharmacologic management of cardiac arrest patients is widely debated; however, several studies published in the past 5 years have begun to clarify some of these issues. This article covers the current state of evidence for the effectiveness of the vasopressor epinephrine and the combination of vasopressin-steroids-epinephrine and antiarrhythmic medications amiodarone and lidocaine and reviews the role of other medications such as calcium, sodium bicarbonate, magnesium, and atropine in cardiac arrest care. We additionally review the role of β-blockers for refractory pulseless ventricular tachycardia/ventricular fibrillation and thrombolytics in undifferentiated cardiac arrest and suspected fatal pulmonary embolism.

articles.title: Endpoint-specific mortality associated with malignancy among adults with sepsis or septic shock: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Sepsis is a major global health challenge and increasingly affects patients with complex conditions such as malignancy. Prior studies suggest higher mortality in this population, but interpretation is limited by aggregation of heterogeneous endpoints. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to clarify endpoint-specific prognostic associations between malignancy and mortality in adults with sepsis or septic shock. This study was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251141216). PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library and Epistemonikos were searched through 16 September 2025, for studies comparing all-cause mortality between sepsis patients with and without malignancy. Mortality endpoints were grouped as ICU, in-hospital, early, intermediate and extended follow-up mortality. Crude odds ratios (ORs) were estimated using random-effects meta-analysis. Subgroup, meta-regression and sensitivity analyses were performed to explore heterogeneity and assess consistency. Among 105 eligible studies comprising 20,089,138 participants, 85 studies contributing 101 endpoint estimates were included in the primary synthesis. articles.title: Peripheral Vasopressor Administration: An Evidence-Based Risk-Benefit Analysis.
articles.abstract: Peripheral vasopressor administration has been heavily researched over the past decade as a way to quickly treat hemodynamically unstable patients. However, current evidence is diverse and limited by quality concerns, including a reliance on retrospective studies, inconsistent criteria, and bias risk. While central venous access devices (CVADs) remain the preferred route for vasopressor administration, use of the peripheral route is necessary when a CVAD is not yet present or contraindicated. Vascular access selection should be tailored to individual patient's needs. Current evidence indicates that using a protocolized approach for peripheral vasopressors appears safe and effective for low-acuity patients requiring short-term therapy (eg, less than 24 hours).

articles.title: Advancing ventilation during cardiopulmonary resuscitation: a question of optimizing quality, ventilation parameters or both?
articles.abstract: Ventilation is provided to most patients during cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR). International guidelines emphasize the need for effective intra-arrest ventilation while acknowledging uncertainty regarding the optimal ventilation parameters. This review will discuss how new studies challenge prior beliefs on key ventilation parameters, will highlight challenges and potential solutions for high-quality ventilation and will suggest a translational research approach to advance intra-arrest ventilation. A recent observational study reported that higher ventilation rates during in-hospital cardiac arrest may be positively associated with return of spontaneous circulation, challenging common beliefs. Additionally, a pivotal observational study on bag-valve-mask ventilation during out-of-hospital cardiac arrest found that ventilation was frequently ineffective and if so, associated with reduced survival and neurological function. Scoping and systematic reviews on intra-arrest ventilation parameters, ventilation feedback devices and mechanical ventilation have uncovered uncertainties regarding fundamental aspects of intra-arrest ventilation. articles.title: Prone positioning in acute respiratory distress syndrome: A critical review of clinical evidence and practical challenges.
articles.abstract: Early randomised controlled trials (RCTs) of prone positioning (PP) in acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) failed to demonstrate a survival benefit despite consistent improvements in oxygenation. Subsequent meta-analyses suggested a survival advantage in patients with severe hypoxaemia, culminating in the landmark Proning Severe ARDS Patients (PROSEVA) trial, which reported a 28-day mortality rate of 16.0% in patients with a PaO₂/FiO₂ ratio <150 mmHg. However, the optimal criteria for repeating and discontinuing PP sessions remain uncertain. A structured search of PubMed, Embase.com, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) was conducted to identify RCTs evaluating PP in adults with ARDS with mortality as a prespecified principal outcome. Relevant clinical studies, meta-analyses, and review articles were also evaluated to provide context for the narrative review. Six RCTs were included in the main comparative analysis. Previous RCTs conducted before the PROSEVA trial used diverse protocols and treatment settings and did not demonstrate a survival benefit. articles.title: Intravenous Immunoglobulin Administration in Cardiac Surgery, Heart Transplantation and Infective Endocarditis: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract: Perioperative infections are a common cause of morbidity in cardiac surgery. Intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) is increasingly used as a rescue treatment for septic shock. However, data on efficacy and safety in cardiac surgery patients are limited. A scoping review of available literature aimed at identifying studies investigating the use of IVIG in patients undergoing cardiac surgery or with infective endocarditis was performed. Studies reporting data on the use of IVIG in these populations were included, including case reports. Data on study design, population, control group, indications for IVIG therapy, and formulation and dose of IVIG were abstracted. Outcome data from randomized controlled trials (RCTs) were also abstracted. A total of 135 studies were identified, including 7 RCTs and 1 RCT study protocol. Most studies were performed in the setting of heart transplantation, followed by nontransplant cardiac surgery and infective endocarditis. The most common formulation was standard IVIG at a dose of 2 g/kg. articles.title: Triptolide-loaded MSC membrane nanoparticles with enhanced pulmonary accumulation for the treatment of acute lung injury: from network pharmacology to experimental validation.
articles.abstract: Acute lung injury (ALI) and its severe form acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) are critical conditions with few effective therapies. Triptolide (TPL), a bioactive compound from Tripterygium wilfordii, exhibits potent anti-inflammatory effects but its clinical use is restricted by poor solubility, rapid clearance, and hepatotoxicity. Using network pharmacology and molecular docking as hypothesis-generating approaches, we prioritized NLRP3 inflammasome activation as a key candidate pathway mediating the therapeutic effects of TPL against ALI. Based on this, we developed mesenchymal stem cell membrane-coated TPL-loaded biomimetic nanoparticles (CM@TPL-NPs) comprising a PLGA core loaded with TPL and coated with mesenchymal stem cell membranes. This coating improved biocompatibility, reduced hepatic sequestration, and enabled preferential lung accumulation, while retaining inherent anti-inflammatory activity. CM@TPL-NPs showed favorable physicochemical properties, sustained release, and improved biocompatibility. articles.title: Effects of protein, muscle rehabilitation and trunk neuromuscular electrostimulation in patients with prolonged mechanical ventilation: a prospective, randomized controlled pilot study.
articles.abstract: Attenuating diaphragmatic dysfunction is important in patients with prolonged mechanical ventilation (PMV). The clinical impact of protein supplementation, core muscle rehabilitation and neuromuscular electrostimulation (NMES) in patients with PMV remains unknown. We conducted a single center, prospective, randomized controlled pilot study for critically ill patients with PMV . All enrolled patients were randomly assigned into four groups: (1) usual care (UC) + high-protein diet (HP); (2) UC + HP + core muscle rehabilitation; (3) UC + HP + core muscle rehabilitation + NMES; and (4) UC. The interventions were maintained for 21 days. Primary outcomes were successful weaning from the ventilator and the duration of mechanical ventilation. Secondary outcomes were length of hospital stay and in-hospital mortality. A total of 100 patients were enrolled, with 10 in the UC group and 30 each in the other three groups. Nine patients discontinued the trial early. The mean compliance rates of core muscle rehabilitation and NMES were nearly 90%. articles.title: Management of shock phenotypes after cardiac arrest: beyond cardiogenic shock.
articles.abstract: Postcardiac-arrest circulatory failure is commonly labeled cardiogenic shock, although its physiology is heterogeneous, dynamic, and frequently mixed. This review examines recent evidence and proposes a treatment-oriented framework. Hypotension, hyperlactatemia, vasopressor dependence, and myocardial dysfunction do not establish ongoing shock after cardiac arrest or identify its mechanism. Recent studies demonstrate clinically important discordance between arterial pressure, cardiac output, filling pressures, oxygen transport, metabolic recovery, and prognosis. Four primary hemodynamic phenotypes are proposed: vasoplegic-inflammatory shock; myocardial dysfunction and low-flow shock; hypovolemia; and right ventricular and pulmonary vascular dysfunction. Mixed shock is an overlap group, whereas reversible metabolic pseudoshock describes arrest-related hyperlactatemia that resolves without persistent hemodynamic compromise. Repeated multimodal assessment should determine whether circulatory dysfunction is resolving or persisting and identify the dominant mechanism. articles.title: Comparison of subanaesthetic ketamine and lidocaine as adjuvants to propofol-based total intravenous anesthesia on propofol requirement during emergency decompressive craniectomy for traumatic brain injury: a prospective, double-blind, three-arm randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: Prevention of secondary brain injury remains a key objective during emergency decompressive craniectomy for traumatic brain injury (TBI). Propofol-based total intravenous anesthesia (TIVA) is widely used in TBI because of its favorable cerebral physiological effects but may cause dose-dependent hypotension and compromise cerebral perfusion. Ketamine and lidocaine have been proposed as adjuncts that may reduce anesthetic requirements while preserving intracranial homeostasis. This study compared the effects of ketamine and lidocaine versus placebo on propofol consumption and perioperative intracranial pressure (ICP), cerebral perfusion pressure (CPP), and brain relaxation during TIVA in patients undergoing emergency decompressive craniectomy for TBI. In this prospective, double-blind, three-arm randomized controlled trial, 150 adults undergoing emergency decompressive craniectomy for traumatic acute subdural hematoma were randomized to receive adjunctive ketamine (0.5 mg/kg/h), lidocaine (2 mg/kg/h), or placebo during propofol-based TIVA. articles.title: Albumin and the kidney, a friend or foe.
articles.abstract: Albumin preparations are the most common colloids used in critically ill patients worldwide. This review is to provide the physiological rationale and evidence for benefits and harms in different clinical settings. There is a strong physiological rationale for intravenous albumin administration in critically ill patients. Iso-oncotic and hyperoncotic albumin have both been used for volume resuscitation and to maintain effective plasma volume at an optimal fluid balance. This practice, however, has not proven to be superior to using crystalloids or balanced solutions with no significant reduction in kidney injury or time on vasopressors. In patients with septic shock and hypoalbuminaemia, albeit limitations, subgroup analysis of a randomized trial suggested reduced mortality with albumin supplementation. Similarly, guidelines strongly recommend the use of albumin in hepatic-induced kidney injury and hepatorenal syndrome. Albumin also improved diuresis when combined with diuretics and may improve intradialytic hypotension.
